question.text: For a Merger Arbitrage Strategy, the investment manager needs to estimate fair value of the premium paid. This estimation primarily impacts:

answer.text: The expense ratio of the fund.
The Conversion Ratio implied and hence the long/short position sizing in target and acquirer.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 10.1.4.2: fair-value estimate of premium determines implied conversion ratio, which drives sizing of long target / short-or-long acquirer legs. Wrong conversion ratio estimate = wrong sizing = arb doesn't converge. **The Trap:** A, C, D are unrelated to spread math. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C same. XV tests intrinsic-value work. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For full-stock deals, anchor on the announced conversion ratio. For cash-stock hybrid deals, decompose into cash-element (collect carry) and stock-element (swap math). Don't assume one ratio fits both — misallocation shows up as spread widening pre-close.
